body:
Reproduced.

In [UrlRule.php:170](https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/web/UrlRule.php#L170) regexp `\w` is too strict and causes incorrect rule parsing.

![screenshot from 2015-10-26 12 53 31](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/4499203/10727188/98352a24-7be0-11e5-96b8-b888bf307a67.png)
@SilverFire thanks for finding the cause, could you fix it and send a PR?
Yes, that's an option. I'd go for it.
It could make routing a bit slower though...

issue.title: Fixed `yii\web\UrlRule` to allow route parameter names with `-`, `_`, `.` characters

body: I have similar problems using hyphens in my URL. The URL manager contains the following rule: post/slug:[w\-]+ , going to /post/slug-value-1 works as expected but when I try to create a URL linking to this page using Html::a('view post', ['post', 'slug' => $model['slug']]) it fails when there is more than 1 hypen/dash in the url. A slug with value "slug-1" works, but "slug-value-1" fails. I have tried different regular expressions, the route works fine but creating the url fails. I found that simply specifying post/<slug> in the URL manager works as expected. (I am not sure, but this might be related to this bug)
